subject: Technical deep-dive recap — latency & throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.com>, Priya Ramachandran <pri.ram@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep-dive recap — latency & throughput SLOs

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the detailed walk-through of Acme's production inference pain points. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, our initial read on fit, and proposed next steps. I attached an SLO worksheet (slo-requirements.xlsx) with the items below filled out — please review and flag anything we missed.

Summary of customer goals / pain points
- Latency spikes: p95 tail spikes up to ~3s during peak batches (affects UI latency and user experience)
- Throughput: sustained background batch jobs (embedding/processing) plus bursty low-latency front-end requests (mixed workload)
- Cost: current spend on dedicated infra is growing; looking to reduce per-token cost without regressing quality
- Compliance: need SOC2 evidence and VPC deployment option for prod data

SLO targets discussed (customer targets in bold)
- Short prompts (<=512 tokens): target p95 <= 200 ms (customer target) — realistic p50 ~60-120 ms
- Long context (4k–8k): target p95 <= 600 ms for standard requests
- Throughput: baseline 200–300 RPS for normal traffic, burst capacity to 800–1,000 RPS for short windows
- Availability: 99.95% regional SLA for inference endpoints

Model & workload constraints
- Primary model: ~8k context window; prefer open/quantizable model family that supports int8/4 quantization for cost savings
- Determinism: some user flows need consistent outputs for rerank/cacheability (avoid aggressive temperature)
- Token mix: mixed short prompts + long-context embeddings; KV-cache reuse expected for chat history patterns

Recommended deployment topology (initial proposal)
- Dedicated cluster in us-east1 for primary production traffic (autoscaling pool sized for baseline throughput + 2x buffer)
- Hot path: low-latency optimized nodes (bfloat16/int8 kernel) with aggressive prefix/KV caching for short prompts
- Cold path / cost fallback: hosted Redwood model variants (smaller quantized model) for non-critical/background jobs and surge overflow
- Multi-region failover: replicate to us-central as secondary for region-level outage tolerance

Open questions we flagged (please confirm)
- Current concurrency per-client and any hard rate limits enforced today
- Typical prompt lengths distribution (we captured sampled percentiles but want production confirmation)
- Procurement/compliance timeline for SOC2 evidence and VPC onboarding

Action items / next steps
- Marissa: schedule a technical PoC kick-off (target next week), provide deployment-topologies.pdf and cost estimator by EOD Tue (attached)
- Acme (Sam / Priya): share a small representative request set and 24–72h production trace sample (to validate batching/prefix cache gains)
- Lauren: prepare infra checklist and firewall/VPC requirements for the PoC

Thanks — happy to sync live if it's easier to walk through the worksheet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: slo-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Ramachandran <pri.ram@acme.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap — latency & throughput SLOs

Thanks Marissa — this is excellent and captures the discussion. A few clarifications from our side:

- The ~3s tail spikes are what we see in the UI for certain user journeys (search + summarization combo). They happen ~2–3x per hour during peak and are the main customer complaint right now.
- Concurrency per client is variable but typical mid-tier tenants hit ~50 concurrent requests; our aggregate concurrency across customers peaks ~600–700.
- Prompt length distribution: ~70% short (<256 tokens), 25% medium (256–2k), 5% long (2k–8k). We'll export samples and the 48h trace you requested.

We are very interested in a PoC. Two asks before we can commit to a timeline:
1) Can you provide a rough cost estimator (ballpark VPS/GPU minutes + expected per-million token cost) for the dedicated cluster + fallback hosted mix?
2) We need SOC2 Type II evidence and a short network/VPC onboarding checklist (so our security team can start the review).

If it helps, we can do a 45-minute PoC scoping call on Wed 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Sam
Director of Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
sam.torres@acme.com

Sam — great, thanks for the additional color and the sample distributions. Outline below to confirm next steps and dates:

PoC scope & timeline
- Objective: validate p95 latency improvements for short prompts and cost reduction via quantized model + batching/caching
- Success criteria: p95 short-prompt <= 200 ms in dedicated cluster under representative load; end-to-end cost-per-1M tokens reduction >= 30% vs your current baseline
- Duration: 2 weeks (1 week setup + baseline test, 1 week load/validation)

Pre-PoC deliverables (we'll provide)
- Deployment topology diagrams and runbook (deployment-topologies.pdf attached)
- Ballpark cost estimator (per-1M tokens + hourly cluster cost) — sending in separate doc by EOD Tue
- SOC2 artifact packet + VPC onboarding checklist (linked in HubSpot record)

Asked from Acme
- Representative request set + 48h request trace (Sam / Priya)
- Test account details and any IP allowlist info for VPC peering
- Point-of-contact for networking and security (name + email)

I've attached deployment-topologies.pdf and linked the HubSpot deal where we'll track the PoC (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567). Lauren & Ethan — can you review the runbook and cost estimator and flag any infra constraints by EOD Tue so we can confirm Wed scoping call?

Proposed Wed scoping: Wed 2027-06-23 10:00am PT — Sam / Priya / Marissa / Lauren / Ethan. Sam — please confirm if that works and we'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa
